Genie Z-135/70 · S/N Z13513-1861 Field procedure

Bringing the Axles In

The machine measured 12.8 ft at the yard and the trailer would not take it. That is the axles fully extended. Here is how to get them back in — the normal way, the way that still works when the control modules are faulted, and what to do if neither lands.

Axles out
12 ft 11 in
Axles in
8 ft 1 in
You gain
4 ft 10 in
Plate weight
45,264 lb
Top: as it sits, axles extended. Bottom: axles retracted, inside a standard 8 ft 6 in deck. OM p.64
What’s holding them out Do the faults block it? Route A · Platform If it won’t drive Route B · Power unit Route C · Move it wide After

01What is holding the axles out

Hydraulically: they are locked, not just parked

Two axle extension cylinders — one across the front pair of axle arms, one across the rear (98147GT, qty 2). Each one carries two counterbalance valves: front DB/DC, rear DD/DE, cross-piloted, 3:1 pilot ratio, set at 3000 psi.

What that means on the ground: you cannot push the axles in, and you cannot let them drift in by cracking a hose. The valve on the far side stays shut until it sees pilot pressure from the opposite line. The only thing that moves an axle is oil pushed into the retract side under real pressure.

Electrically: three permissives

  1. Booms stowed. “The axles can only be retracted if the primary and secondary booms are fully lowered and retracted and the platform is between the circle-end wheels.” OM p.48
  2. Drive enable light off. “When the drive enable light is on, the axles cannot retract.” OM p.51
  3. Platform controls only, drive handle moved. “Drive, steer and axle functions are not available from the ground controls.” OM p.48
The safety mechanism points the other way

LSFA1ES and LSRA1ES — the front and rear axle extended safety switches — prevent boom functions with the axles retracted. They close when the axles are fully out. SM p.203

So the interlock guards against booming up on a narrow track. It does not guard against retracting a stowed machine — that is the intended, normal operation. There is no ground-control axle button, no bypass-mode axle function and no recovery-mode axle function. Bypass is for a platform out-of-level condition and calibration. Recovery retracts the primary boom, retracts the secondary boom and lowers the primary boom — booms only. SM pp.100–101

02Do this machine’s faults block the retract?

Checked line by line against the Control System Fault Code table. Only one of the eleven matters — and it matters a lot.

Fault on the displayWhat the manual says it disablesBlocks retract?
Front axle angle sensor 0 V p.184Primary up, secondary up/down and extendNo
Rear axle angle sensor 0 V p.185SameNo
LF / RF / LR / RR steer sensor 0 V pp.186–187SameNo
Primary boom angle sensor not calibrated p.184Primary up only active from TCONNot directly
Secondary boom angle sensor not calibratedBoom functionsNot directly
Secondary boom switch fault, LSS1RS p.188Inhibits secondary boom downNot directly
SCON CAN no response p.176Display message on LCDNot directly
Primary boom angle zone fault p.189SCON matrix row Primary boom angle (crosscheck) switches OFF P_38, P_39, P_10, P_11, P_30Possibly
Read that last row twice

P_38 is the switched safety power to propel. If the SCON has latched the primary-boom-angle crosscheck, the machine will not drive — and axle motion is commanded with the drive handle, so no drive usually means no axle motion either.

The two SCON rows that actually mention axles — axle safety not stowed and axle crosscheck angle sensor versus safety switch — switch off P_39, P_10, P_11 and P_30, but not P_38. The axle sensors reading 0 V do not, on their own, kill propel. SM p.189

Which gives you one clean test

If the machine drives, the axles will almost certainly retract. That is the first thing to try.

Route ARetract from the platform

About twenty minutes. No tools. Two people — one on the controls, one watching the wheels.

Booms stowed first — eyeball it, don’t trust the display

Primary boom fully down and fully retracted. Secondary boom fully down and fully retracted. Jib stowed. Platform sitting between the two circle-end wheels. If any of that is not true, stop and get the booms stowed. Narrowing the track with a boom in the air is the exact tip-over the interlocks exist to prevent.

  1. A – 1Firm, level ground

    Not a soft shoulder, not a slope. Walk the four wheel wells: nothing jammed in the axle slides, no frozen mud packed in, bellows not shredded, no chain or strap threaded through the arms.

  2. A – 2Turntable rotation lock pin out

    It goes back in for transport, not now.

  3. A – 3Clear 15 to 20 feet fore and aft

    The machine rolls while the axles move. That is deliberate — it lets the tires roll instead of scrubbing sideways.

  4. A – 4Key to platform control, both E-stops out

    Ground box and platform box. Start the engine from the platform. Do not stand on the foot switch while cranking.

  5. A – 5The propel test

    Foot switch down, drive handle gently forward. It creeps → propel power is live, carry on. Nothing, alarm sounds → propel is cut, go to the next section.

  6. A – 6Drive enable light must be off

    If it is on, the primary boom has swung past a circle-end wheel and the axles will not come in. Rotate the turntable so the boom sits between the circle-end wheels and the light goes out. OM p.51

  7. A – 7Foot switch down, hold the drive handle

    Either direction. The machine will creep — that is correct.

  8. A – 8While holding it, activate retract axle

    On the toggle-switch panel it is the axle extend/retract switch, item 24. On the button panel it is the axle retract button, item 31. The retract symbol is the one with the arrows pointing inward.

  9. A – 9Hold until the light goes steady

    The indicator flashes while the axles move and stays on when they are fully retracted. OM p.48 Your second person watches both ends — all four wheels should come in together. If one end moves and the other does not, that end needs Route B.

  10. A – 10Measure

    You are looking for 8 ft 1 in.

If it moves partway and stops

Let it sit thirty seconds and try again — the pump may be catching up. Hot oil helps: run at high idle for five minutes. Creep the machine forward and back a few feet between attempts to unload the tires. [F]

03If the machine will not drive

Then propel power P_38 is switched off and the SCON is the thing switching it. Cheapest checks first:

  1. Cycle the power properly. Engine off, both E-stops in, key off, wait sixty seconds, then key on, E-stops out, restart. A lot of these are latched history rather than live faults.
  2. Read the fault list again after the cycle. Only the ones that come back are live.
  3. Look for a boom-angle-zone message. If the primary boom angle sensor is what is holding P_38 off, the fix is the sensor circuit, not the axles — that is the main diagnosis, and the leading suspect there is the P21DCON feed out of TCON J12-2.
  4. Get the boom angle circuit healthy and propel comes back, and Route A works.
What not to do

Do not jumper, jump or hot-wire the axle retract solenoid coil at J100, and do not tape the axle extended limit switches closed. That chain is what stops the axles coming in with a boom in the air. Route B gets you the same result with the booms verified stowed first, under your own hand at the cylinder — and it is Genie’s own documented method.

Route BPortable hydraulic power unit at the cylinder

This is Genie’s documented way to move an axle extension cylinder with no machine control power. It lives inside SM 10-3, “How to Remove an Axle Extension Cylinder”. You use steps 1–4 and 8, and skip the pin removal in 5–7 because you are not removing anything.

“Connect the hydraulic hoses from a portable hydraulic power unit to the axle extension cylinder. Note: Connect the pressure hose from the power unit to the ‘R’ port of the cylinder and the return hose from the power unit to the ‘E’ port on the cylinder.” SM p.164

R is the retract side, E is the extend side. Pressure into R pilots the opposite counterbalance valve open and pulls that axle pair in.

What you need

  • Portable hydraulic power unit or hand pump good for 2000+ psi with usable volume, plus two hoses that fit the cylinder ports
  • Caps and plugs for the machine-side hoses and the cylinder fittings
  • Fresh O-rings for every fitting you break SM p.164
  • Drip pans, rags, chocks, gloves, eye protection
  • Two people

  1. B – 1Verify the booms are stowed

    Primary down and in, secondary down and in, jib stowed, platform between the circle-end wheels. Eyeball it. If a boom is up, stop.

  2. B – 2Firm, level ground, stowed position

    The manual’s own precondition for this procedure. SM p.164

  3. B – 3Chock all four wheels

    OM p.58

  4. B – 4Engine off, both E-stops in, key in your pocket

  5. B – 5Find the cylinder for the end you are doing

    Parts Manual p.20, “201.1 Top View”, item 10 shows both cylinders and where they sit. Item 9 is the axle extension limit switch.

  6. B – 6Tag, disconnect and plug the hoses. Cap the cylinder fittings

    From the manual: spraying hydraulic oil can penetrate and burn skin. Loosen connections very slowly to let the pressure bleed off. Do not let oil squirt or spray.

  7. B – 7Remove the axle extension limit switch cover and switch

    Leave the wiring connected. The manual does this; it costs four fasteners and it protects the actuator block. SM p.164

  8. B – 8Pressure hose to R. Return hose to E

    Get this the right way round. R pulls the axles in.

  9. B – 9Raise pressure slowly

    The axle pair on that end will start to come in. Watch both arms.

  10. B – 10Cap it at about 2400 psi

    That is the machine’s own axle relief setting, 2400 psi / 165 bar. SM p.5 If it will not move at that pressure the tires are scrubbing — do not crank it higher. [M]

  11. B – 11Run it to the stop, release pressure, do the other end

    One cylinder per end. Both must come in.

  12. B – 12Reconnect with new O-rings, torqued to spec

    Reinstall the limit switch and cover. Start the engine, look for leaks, top up the hydraulic oil.

The part nobody tells you

With the machine’s own controls the axles retract while the machine drives, so the tires roll. With the power-unit method the machine stands still, so the tires have to scrub sideways across whatever they are parked on. On pavement it works. On gravel or dirt it can stall outright. Smooth, hard, flat — and greased steel plates under the tires if you have them — is the difference between a two-hour job and a bad afternoon. [F]/[M]

Route CMove it wide

If neither route gets the axles in, the machine still ships.

  • Oversize permit. In Alberta a 12 ft 11 in load is a routine over-dimensional permit with pilot cars, not an exotic move. Confirm with the carrier before you commit to it.
  • The right trailer. 45,264 lb on the plate. A lowboy with a removable gooseneck, deck width to suit, enough axles.
  • Crane it. Four lifting points on the chassis, booms and jib fully lowered and retracted, all loose items off. OM p.60
  • Winch it on, free-wheeling. Chock the wheels, release the wheel brakes by turning over all four drive hub disconnect caps, secure the winch line to the drive chassis tie points. Reverse to re-engage. The pump free-wheel valve stays closed. OM p.58

04Once the axles are in

  • The booms are locked out, and that is correct. With the axles retracted the primary will not raise, the secondary will not raise, the primary will not extend, and the turntable stops at 15°. That is LSFA1ES and LSRA1ES doing their job. Do not chase it as a new fault. OM pp.31–32
  • It steers wider. Outside turning radius goes from 18 ft 6 in extended to 25 ft 6 in retracted. Give yourself room on the ramp. OM p.64
  • Load it promptly. A Z-135 on a narrow track is far less stable than on a wide one. Do not leave it parked retracted on a slope, and do not boom it up.
  • Rotation lock pin in before it rolls. OM pp.58–59
  • Secure it: minimum six chains of ample capacity on the chassis; a block under the platform rotator, not touching the platform cylinder; a nylon strap through the lower platform support without excessive downward force. OM p.59

Non-negotiables

Never retract the axles with a boom raised or extended. Never jumper or defeat the axle retract solenoid, the LSFA1ES / LSRA1ES limit switches, the axle angle sensors, the tilt sensor or the load cell. Never work beside a cylinder still under pressure — bleed it slowly. Never adjust the axle relief above 2400 psi to force movement. Chock the wheels before any hydraulic work.
